title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
This is a fabricated depiction of a real person published as documentary imagery. The alteration happened in the production of campus banner advertising, downstream of an original photograph taken at a Lunar New Year event, and it changed the identity of one student and the bodies of others. The image was then presented to the public as a photograph of Stanford students, with no indication that it had been synthesised or edited.

Catching it would have required a review step that compared the published image against the source photograph before it went to print, and a check that the material complied with the university's own rule against using A.I. to alter images of Stanford people. Stanford has said the alteration and the absence of disclosure violated that policy, and that it is now arranging training and proper review of all materials, which indicates neither was in place when the banners were produced.

What is not established is intent. The reports do not say who made the edit, which tool was used, or whether anyone faced consequences, and the university's acknowledgement covers the alteration and the policy breach rather than any motive behind them.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic senior majoring in human biology at Stanford, appeared in a 2024 Lunar New Year photo with two other students. The university's dining service posted it online. When Stanford used the image on campus banners last week, Ramirez had been replaced by an image of a Black woman, and the other students were altered to look thinner. Ramirez learned about the change from a friend and said it was upsetting.

Stanford acknowledged on Tuesday that it used artificial intelligence to change the original image. The university said its policy strictly prohibits using A.I. to produce or alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements. It said the alteration and the lack of disclosure violated that policy. Stanford added that it is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to provide more training and ensure proper review of all materials.
title_en: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad
